A1.justification: Both PDFs describe YOSO and its self-cooperative diffusion-GAN framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: v4 reports original CIFAR-10 experiments, text-to-image and LoRA evaluations, component ablations, downstream applications, and an appendix quick-adaptation study.

after.justification: v5 reports original CIFAR-10 training and fine-tuning results, text-to-image evaluations, quantitative component ablations, and downstream demonstrations.

M1.justification: v5 introduces annealing of KL and consistency-loss weights to zero and extends the decoupled scheduler, already present for text-to-image in v4, to CIFAR-10 training. These change the training procedure. v4's explicit YOSO-LoRA-v2 data-flywheel retraining procedure is no longer presented.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, JourneyDB, the HPS benchmark, and the principal generation and downstream tasks remain. v5 adds COCO-5k evaluation and reports internally collected data for LoRA training in Appendix G.2, although that collection's composition is unspecified.

E2.justification: v5 adds Tract, Diff-Instruct, DMD, CTM, and SiD to CIFAR-10 comparisons. Text-to-image comparisons add Hyper-SD-LoRA, PeRFlow, TCD-LoRA, PixArt-DMD, and additional base-model controls. SDXL-Turbo and StyleGAN2 without ADA disappear, as does the budget-matched CT/iCT comparison; standard CT/iCT results remain.

E3.justification: Main CIFAR-10 experiments switch from DDGAN-style networks with LPIPS to EDM networks with MSE and add pretrained-EDM fine-tuning; the smaller architecture remains for ablations. Text-to-image evaluation adds ImageReward and CLIPScore and changes the stated non-HPS evaluation corpus to COCO-5k. Reported LoRA batch size changes from 64 to 128, although Appendix G.2 still states 256.

E4.justification: v5 Tables 3-4 add scheduler and annealing ablations on CIFAR-10 and quantitative text-to-image tests of perceptual loss, IPI, adversarial formulations, and training strategies. Qualitative comparison and application cases are revised. The compute-matched analysis and data-flywheel study disappear, while the discriminator-loss plot and Appendix F quick-adaptation study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark outcomes. The discriminator training curves do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4's CIFAR-10 FID 3.82 survives as YOSO-Base; v5 adds 3.30 and 3.05 in the smaller-backbone ablations and 2.26 from scratch and 1.81 with EDM fine-tuning. PixArt HPS changes from 29.83 to 30.52, and one-step LoRA HPS from 23.34 to 28.33. These span revised training conditions. ImageReward/CLIPScore results are added, while full SD1.5 fine-tuning, budget-matched, and data-flywheel results are removed.

T1.justification: v5 adds Proposition 1 and Appendix C, arguing that the cooperative adversarial loss has a data-matching global optimum under sufficient model capacity. This is a focused theoretical addition to the largely retained probabilistic definitions and derivations.

C1.justification: v5's abstract explicitly claims state-of-the-art one-step performance even with LoRA, whereas v4 claimed high-quality LoRA generation. The explicit first one-step diffusion-transformer claim is dropped. The central self-cooperative generation and zero-shot 512-to-1024 resolution-transfer contributions remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds capacity-based motivation for annealing, timestep-approximation reasoning for decoupled schedules, and a data-versus-teacher explanation for outperforming EDM. It discusses possible human-feedback metric bias and revises mode-collapse interpretations toward DMD and SD-Turbo. The data-flywheel interpretation is removed; Appendix B's general limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 newly supplies a code repository link, a CIFAR-10 fine-tuning learning rate, and additional evaluation-data instructions. Most optimizer and EMA details remain. It removes the explicit CIFAR-10 training-budget table and Appendix C safeguards disclosure, including synthetic-data filtering details; LoRA data-generator provenance becomes less explicit.

R1.justification: Related-work positioning is updated around SDXL-Lightning, Hyper-SD, and Diff-Instruct, with additional references supporting the new baselines, metrics, and COCO evaluation. The central distinction between self-cooperative clean-data matching and other diffusion-GAN formulations remains. Citation-style changes and relocation of related work are presentational.

P1.justification: v5 substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, moves related work from Section 2 to Section 7, and creates a dedicated CIFAR-10 section before text-to-image scaling. LoRA discussion is integrated into the main evaluation, and the application section is shortened. Author, affiliation, header, and citation formatting also change.

P2.justification: v5 reorganizes CIFAR-10 results into main and ablation tables, replaces separate text-to-image tables with a backbone-grouped table containing additional metric columns, and removes the cost and data-flywheel tables. Qualitative comparison and application figures are substantially replaced or reorganized. Figure 1 and the quick-adaptation images are retained within a different document layout.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens evidence for the central method through comparisons using matching backbones and quantitative text-to-image component ablations, addressing v4's limited evidence isolating its scaling techniques. CIFAR-10 ablations also separate the effects of the added training strategies. Removing compute-matched comparisons and weakening some training-data documentation are material losses, but the improved experimental support is substantial; this judgment does not rely on treating revised-setting scores as direct performance gains.
